decisions: RoutineRegistration carries RoutineTypeId only: RoutineParameterCatalog has no code->id lookup. Application must resolve the id; ForCode is not possible.
Odometer reading evaluates with LastTimeEvaluationDate without advancing it (D-04 and odometer-ingestion spec), not with the Bogota date of the reading as the task text says.
Domain events carry OccurredAt without a clock: reading.ReadAt for readings, Bogota start of the effective date for register and reevaluate.
PagedResult<T> did not exist in BuildingBlocks; created in Application/Abstractions (ns ...Application.Abstractions) with Items, Page, PageSize, TotalCount.
Commands without a natural value return the aggregate id (VehicleId/RoutineId/AlertId/RoutineTypeId); no Unit type exists. Plate in commands and DTOs is a plain string.
OdometerReadingLogEntry is an Application record (VehicleId, Kilometers, ReadAt, ReceivedAt, Outcome, IgnoredReason) per ADR-0025; Infrastructure should map it to its own persistence class.
RoutineSnapshot.EffectiveDueSoonPercent (int in V1) is mapped from the decimal snapshot value with Math.Round AwayFromZero.
MaintenanceRoutineRestartedV1.ServicedAt is built from ServiceRecord.Date at 00:00 UTC (DateTimeOffset), since the domain keeps a DateOnly.
The mappers are public sealed classes with a parameterless constructor; the DI registration (scan or manual) is up to whoever owns the DependencyInjection file.

decisions: ReevaluatePlans handler uses ambient plan/routineType repos (same DbContext), no own save: interceptor rounds persist; GetCatalogAsync must return tracked changed RoutineType (new values).
Suspend() has no time input: MaintenancePlanStatusChanged.OccurredAt = Bogota start of LastTimeEvaluationDate; Resume uses start of max(today, Last).
UpdateRoutineOverrides always emits RoutineParametersChanged; ChangeRoutineState and Suspend/Resume emit nothing on a repeated state; evaluation is skipped for inactive routines or suspended plans.
RecordOdometerReadingHandler injects plans, catalog, IOdometerReadingLog, IIntegrationEventPublisher and IUnitOfWork from DI (one shared DbContext), not via scope factory.
Infra: IUnitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync must clear the ChangeTracker on Concurrency.Conflict so the retry reloads the plan and drops the failed log/outbox rows.
Translator and SingleRetry are static classes (no DI registration); conflict is detected by code Concurrency.Conflict (Application cannot reference Infrastructure).
Handlers inject IMaintenancePlanRepository, IRoutineTypeRepository, IUnitOfWork and IClock (not IUnitOfWorkScope); these ports must be registered in DI.
Own bulk handler instead of BulkRegistrationHandler (its ICommandHandler<TCommand,Guid> per-row model does not fit). Dry run saves via BulkExecutionScope.For(dryRun).Resolve(unitOfWork).
The 500-row limit is in RegisterRoutinesBulkCommandValidator (code Bulk.TooManyRows), applied by ValidationCommandHandlerDecorator. Row validator is injected as IValidator<RoutineBulkRow>.
Command handlers inject IUnitOfWork (BuildingBlocks) directly, not IUnitOfWorkScope; Infrastructure must register IUnitOfWork in DI for the Plans and Alerts handlers.
Vehicle status mapping: the string Inactive (case-insensitive) maps to Suspended and any other value maps to Active. Unknown plan in VehicleStatusChanged returns NotFound (failure).
Domain event alert handlers use the event OccurredAt as time and do not save. Revert resolves only open DueSoon alerts; restart and deactivation resolve all open alerts of the routine.
Odometer, RoutineOverrides and MaintenanceCycle use ComplexProperty, not OwnsOne: RoutineOverrides.None is shared across routines and OwnsOne wrote NULLs. Same columns. Verified with a scratch run.
RoutineType.DefaultInterval stays OwnsOne because HasData does not support complex properties. Each RoutineType needs its own MaintenanceInterval instance, so tests must not share one.
Alerts.RoutineId has an FK to routines and OdometerReadings.VehicleId an FK to plans (both Restrict, per data-model). Repository tests must save real plans and routines first.
